Crosswalk between OCS-GE (cover and use) and EUNIS Level 2

Source: R/data.R
ref_ocsge_eunis.Rd

Correspondence table between the French OCS-GE nomenclature and the 45 EUNIS Level 2 classes of ref_eunis. The two nomenclatures do not nest: OCS-GE cover (CS) describes what physically covers the ground in 14 classes, while EUNIS describes habitats. The relation is therefore many-to-many, and each OCS-GE class is given a ranked list of EUNIS classes. Rows with a land use code (US) refine the match for a given cover: for instance herbaceous cover (CS2.2.1) is arable land (I1) under agricultural use, but gardens and parks (I2) under residential use.

Usage

data(ref_ocsge_eunis)

Format

A data frame with 152 rows and 7 columns:

code_cs

Character. OCS-GE cover code, as in ref_ocsge$code_cs (e.g. "CS2.2.1").

code_us

Character. OCS-GE use code (e.g. "US1.1"), or NA for the cover-only match, to be used when the use is unknown or has no dedicated row.

code_eunis

Character. EUNIS Level 2 code, as in ref_eunis$code and eunis_species_dict$code_eunis.

rank

Integer. Order of the EUNIS classes within a (code_cs, code_us) group; 1 is the default match.

main_cs

Logical. TRUE on the single row giving the main OCS-GE cover of each EUNIS class (EUNIS to OCS-GE direction, 45 rows).

pct_metaleurop

Numeric. Measured share (%) of the OCS-GE group area falling in this EUNIS class on the Metaleurop site; NA when the group covers less than 10 ha there. See Details.

note

Character. What the match stands for, and what extra data would be needed to resolve it.

Details

rank is an expert reading of the two nomenclatures (CNIG OCS-GE specification and EUNIS habitat definitions). pct_metaleurop is a measurement: OCS-GE polygons of roi_metaleurop were overlaid on the EUNIS raster returned by get_eunis_data. The two columns are not expected to agree closely, because the EUNIS raster has a 100 m pixel carrying one dominant class, while OCS-GE maps objects a few meters wide: a road or a garden usually falls in a pixel classified as buildings (J1, J2). The measurement also only covers the classes present on this site.

Some EUNIS distinctions cannot be recovered from OCS-GE, with or without the use: wetlands (D), grassland types (E1 to E4), standing versus running water (C1, C2), deciduous versus evergreen broadleaved woodland (G1, G2), and crops versus permanent grassland, which share the same cover and the same agricultural use.

The source table and the build script are raw_data/ocsge_eunis_crosswalk.csv and raw_data/build_ref_ocsge_eunis.R of the source repository.

See also

ref_ocsge, ref_eunis, eunis_species_dict, get_ocsge_data_fgb

Examples

data(ref_ocsge_eunis)

# default EUNIS class of each OCS-GE cover
subset(ref_ocsge_eunis, is.na(code_us) & rank == 1)
#>       code_cs code_us code_eunis rank main_cs pct_metaleurop

#> 5   CS1.1.1.2    <NA>         J4    1    TRUE             10
#> 8   CS1.1.2.1    <NA>         J4    1   FALSE              3
#> 23  CS1.1.2.2    <NA>         J6    1    TRUE             NA
#> 24    CS1.2.1    <NA>         H5    1    TRUE              0
#> 36    CS1.2.2    <NA>         C1    1    TRUE              2
#> 52    CS1.2.3    <NA>         H4    1    TRUE             NA
#> 53  CS2.1.1.1    <NA>         G1    1    TRUE             53
#> 66  CS2.1.1.2    <NA>         G3    1    TRUE             NA
#> 76  CS2.1.1.3    <NA>         G4    1    TRUE             NA
#> 86    CS2.1.2    <NA>         F3    1    TRUE              0
#> 100   CS2.1.3    <NA>         FB    1    TRUE             NA
#> 101   CS2.2.1    <NA>         I1    1    TRUE             54
#> 148   CS2.2.2    <NA>         D1    1    TRUE             NA
#>                                                                                   note
#> 1                                                        Buildings of the urban fabric
#> 5                                             Sealed ground: roads, car parks, squares
#> 8                          Railway ballast, gravel tracks, unsealed transport surfaces
#> 23                                              Landfills, dumps, slag and spoil heaps

# main OCS-GE cover of each EUNIS class
subset(ref_ocsge_eunis, main_cs, c(code_eunis, code_cs))

#> 151         F1   CS2.2.2
#> 152         D3   CS2.2.2

# EUNIS class of OCS-GE polygons from cover and use, falling back on cover alone
ocs <- data.frame(code_cs = c("CS2.2.1", "CS2.2.1", "CS2.1.1.1"),
                  code_us = c("US1.1", "US5", "US1.2"))
best <- subset(ref_ocsge_eunis, rank == 1)
with_us <- best$code_eunis[match(paste(ocs$code_cs, ocs$code_us),
                                 paste(best$code_cs, best$code_us))]
cs_only <- best$code_eunis[match(paste(ocs$code_cs, NA),
                                 paste(best$code_cs, best$code_us))]
ocs$code_eunis <- ifelse(is.na(with_us), cs_only, with_us)
ocs
#>     code_cs code_us code_eunis
#> 1   CS2.2.1   US1.1         I1
#> 2   CS2.2.1     US5         I2
#> 3 CS2.1.1.1   US1.2         G1
